id: title:clr182:skip malformed network entries instead of crashing

review.posthog_relevance: Adds a runtime filter in the APM session recording ingestion path to skip malformed `rrweb/network@1` request payloads, preventing potential crashes or skipped recordings when the external recording library sends unexpected structures.
review.reason: The implementation hunk P1.F2.H1 introduces a defensive check that skips non-object entries before processing, which is a substantive, bounded reliability improvement for the session recording ingestion path. The accompanying test P1.F1.H1 only asserts the expected behavior of the skipped entries and does not establish tier or score. This is not a narrow documentation or test-only,
review.uncertainty: This score relies on the assumption that the skipped entries could have caused a crash or significant processing failure; while the code implements a safeguard, the actual production impact depends on the frequency and severity of malformed payloads from the external library, which is not demonstrated in the diff. No adoption or incident avoidance is inferred.

observations.limitations: This chunk contains two hunks. P1.F1.H1 is a test file and P1.F2.H1 is the implementation. P1.F1.H1 does not establish tier or score. P1.F2.H1 establishes a tier. P1.F1.H1 is not included in the score.

observations.behavior: Adds a test asserting that malformed entries in rrweb/network@1 requests are skipped rather than crashing.
observations.posthog_connection: Adds regression test coverage for the malformed-request handling added in P1.F2.H1.

observations.behavior: Adds a filter before mapping to skip entries that are not objects, preventing crashes on malformed rrweb/network@1 request payloads.
observations.posthog_connection: Changes the APM session recording ingestion path to filter out malformed network request entries before processing, improving reliability of session recordings. This could prevent session recording failures or crashes when rrweb sends unexpected payload structures. This is a bounded, implementation-visible improvement.
